subject: Meteorology
title: Cirrocumulus Clouds
description: A fast breakdown of Cirrocumulus Clouds for builders.

hook.text: Cirrocumulus looks like tiny white ripples or grains at high altitude—a delicate pattern that rarely lasts long.

buildup.text: These clouds form above 6 km when shallow instability disrupts a thin ice-crystal layer.

discovery.text: Each cloudlet appears smaller than a finger-width at arm's length—much tinier than altocumulus puffs.

twist.text: Cirrocumulus is the rarest of the ten main cloud types—it usually transforms quickly into cirrus or cirrostratus.

climax.text: When it does appear, it can create a stunning rippled sky that photographers prize for its fleeting beauty.

punchline.text: Blink and you'll miss it—the rarest common cloud.

quiz.question: Why is cirrocumulus considered rare?
options: It transforms quickly into other cloud types
